header:
Date: 2025-04-02
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Tom Reynolds (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Verdigris Head of ML), Ben Cho (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Product), Samir (Data Scientist), Jules (QA)
Recording: Zoom
Notes: Sprint 2 pilot weekly sync focused on regression hunt, prompt bisection, and guardrail false positives. Several failing categories identified; discussed rollback triggers and canary thresholds.
summary: Quick recap: model drift seen on promotional SKU language (templates) leading to hallucinated personalization; a subset of prompts trigger a guardrail false positive (privacy filter). We agreed to bisection on a 300-sample failing set, run targeted A/B at 100k throughput slice, and run a KV-cache stress job to check latency regressions under sustained load. Action owners assigned. Customer asked about data residency and on-prem feasibility; Redwood to surface security docs and pilot SOW.
topics:
1) Regression breakdown by intent and template
2) Bisection plan for prompt set
3) Guardrail tuning and false positive thresholds
4) Performance under sustained cache hits (KV cache)
5) Next steps for pilot expansion and security review
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. appreciate you carving out time. quick check, can folks hear me?
[00:04] Lena Ortiz: Yep loud and clear.
[00:07] Tom Reynolds: good to go from my side.
[00:10] Maya Patel: cool, agenda — sprint two regression hunt, results we pulled overnight, then bisection plan and guardrail adjustments. we'll keep this tight 40 minutes.
[00:20] Ben Cho: before we start — small ask: can you call out which run is the one with the KV-cache enabled? we saw weird latency spread on Friday.
[00:30] Tom Reynolds: yeah that's the run with k v cash — sorry k v cache — enabled with the continuous batching flag. Friday's spike was when we hit the long tail of sequence lengths. i've got notes.
[00:40] Lena Ortiz: high-level — we've got two main failure modes: one is hallucinated personalization on promo templates where the model invents customer-specific discounts. two is guardrail false positives when product descriptions include PII-like tokens (e.g., order numbers). both are blocking.
[00:55] Maya Patel: ok that's great context. tom, can you walk through the regression heatmap?
[01:00] Tom Reynolds: sure. uploaded the heatmap to drive, link in chat. the top clusters — cluster A is promo templates, cluster B is short SKU queries, cluster C is long-form returns where KV-cache gets stale. the interesting bit — the accuracy drop for cluster A correlates with a recent small param quant change and a batching tweak. i suspect the quant profile for embeddings path nudged logits in low-confidence cases.
[01:30] Samir: when you say quant profile did you mean we rolled from 4-bit asymmetric to 4-bit symmetric for that layer?
[01:36] Tom Reynolds: yes that's right, though it was targeted. that said the majority of degradation looks like prompt/template sensitivity rather than catastrophic model change.
[01:45] Priya Nair: are we sure it's not a prompt drift on our side? we pushed a new set of marketing templates last week.
[01:50] Lena Ortiz: we pulled historical logs — same templates were used earlier and had better fidelity, so more likely system side changes but we'll keep both hypotheses.
[02:05] Jules (QA): also flagging there's an intermittent 500 error on the scoring endpoint during high QPS. might be infra timeouts.
[02:13] Ben Cho: yes saw that, it aligns with the KV-cache stress window.
[02:18] Maya Patel: action 1: Tom will run a targeted KV-cache stress job and post latency percentiles. action 2: we will run a bisection on the 300-sample failing set from Lena.
[02:30] Tom Reynolds: for bisection i propose we split by template and model variant; run half on current quant profile and half on previous. that should tell us if quant is causal.
[02:40] Samir: timeline — how long for that?
[02:43] Tom Reynolds: with our infra — couple hours for the 300 samples with full traces, we'll push results end of day tomorrow.
[02:50] Lena Ortiz: good. also on guardrails — we saw false positives for order # patterns. guardrail flagged as PII. is that a strict regex?
[02:58] Tom Reynolds: the guardrail currently uses a mix of regexes and an auxiliary classifier. the classifier threshold has a default conservative setting. we can tune thresholds per customer but need to balance false negatives.
[03:12] Priya Nair: could we get a mode where low-confidence guardrail hits are sent as 'review' instead of blocking? sometimes it's okay to pass through with audit.
[03:20] Maya Patel: yes that's a pattern we support — soft-fail with audit log. Redwood Console can surface those events with token-level context for review. we'll propose a threshold.
[03:30] Ben Cho: important — any change to guardrail thresholds must have rollback triggers. what would those be?
[03:36] Tom Reynolds: recommend automated rollback if precision drops below 92% on a 1k sample probe or if false accept rate increases >1% in production canary. we can codify that in the rollout policy.
[03:48] Lena Ortiz: that sounds reasonable. can you put those metrics in the SOW?
[03:52] Maya Patel: will do.
[03:55] [04:00] (crosstalk)
[04:05] Maya Patel: performance note: Friday's run had a tail latency at p99 1.6 s for 128-token responses with KV cache; without cache it was 2.1s under similar load. we're watching tokenization variance though.
[04:20] Jules (QA): any chance the tokenizer update changed token counts causing longer sequences?
[04:24] Tom Reynolds: maybe — tokenizer mapping changes can increase effective sequence length; that's on the checklist.
[04:30] Ben Cho: about security/on-prem — our security team wants to know if Redwood supports export controls and HSM integration.
[04:38] Maya Patel: yes, we do KMS/HSM integrations and have a private deployment option. i'll share SOC 2 and the on-prem playbook in the follow-up.
[04:46] Lena Ortiz: timeline for pilot expansion — we'd like to move to dedicated pool if the A/B looks good, target start mid-April. cost is a tradeoff.
[04:56] Maya Patel: understood, we'll include pricing and a dedicated capacity proposal in the SOW.
[05:02] Tom Reynolds: one more technical note — when we did continuous batching changes we inadvertently increased the max batch size limit; under certain request mixes that pushes latency for small requests. we can tweak autoscale thresholds to protect small-request SLOs.
[05:20] Priya Nair: can you document those config knobs? we might want to tune them ourselves.
[05:25] Tom Reynolds: yes i'll add a README in the pilot repo.
[05:30] Maya Patel: ok let's do a quick recap of owners. Tom runs KV stress and posts results by 4/7. Lena uploads 300 failed prompts by tomorrow 4/4. Maya sends SOW and security pack by 4/6. Ben shares infra topology by 4/9. any other items?
[05:50] Samir: i'll generate a small labeled set for verification after bisection — can we include that in the evaluation?
[05:55] Tom Reynolds: definitely, that helps calibrate thresholds.
[06:00] Maya Patel: perfect. last thing — customer asked about competitor performance: Anthropic did show better handling of privacy patterns in our public benchmarks but their latency was higher. i want to be transparent.
[06:12] Lena Ortiz: good to know.
[06:15] Maya Patel: alright, thanks everyone. i'll follow up with notes and next steps. see you next week.
[06:20] (meeting ends)
notes: Shared artifacts: drive/verdigris/pilot/heatmap-2025-04-02.png, drive/verdigris/pilot/failing_prompts.csv (pending upload), shared bench doc link. Mentioned SOW, security pack, pricing sheet.
